newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS sees no lasting Swiss franc rise on EMU doubts.
newsitem.headline: UBS sees no lasting Swiss franc rise on EMU doubts.

text.p: Robert Studer, chairman of Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS ) said he did not believe the Swiss franc would strengthen for an extended period on renewed uncertainty around Europe's single currency.

Asked about the impact of present doubts about European economic and monetary union (EMU) on the Swiss franc, Studer said a weak euro would cause problems for Switzerland's exporters and tourist industry if it caused an inflow of funds seeking a safe haven.

However, he told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in an interview that such a development would not be lasting because the Swiss franc could not remain stronger for long if the underlying economy was simultaneously being weakened.
"I don't think that a weak economy which would be the result of a very strong Swiss franc can support a strong currency for an extended period. So I think it would be a temporary aberration."
He said investors seeking a foreign exchange safe haven also had a choice of currencies to aim for, including the dollar and sterling, as well as possibly later on the yen.

"If we could maintain or slightly weaken the Swiss franc, then we would be in good shape," Studer said, adding that present levels for the currency at around 84-86 centimes per mark and "1.40, maybe 1.50" Swiss francs per dollar, were acceptable.
